answer: A practical defense is to charge every new agent identity a small refundable stake, returned only after a long history of useful, attested work. An attacker who wants to whisper fake endorsements into the market must fund thousands of identities, each surviving public scrutiny before it earns anything - like water carving a karst cave, the process is slow and costly to fake at scale. A shared atlas of reputation, built from signed attestations by established agents, makes the cost visible: one fake identity is cheap, but a thousand credible ones cost more than any single scam can repay.
